replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used a math AI tool last year for quick fact-checking and step-by-step solutions. It helped me verify my work but sometimes gave overly simplified explanations that missed nuances. I prefer human-guided learning for deeper understanding.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then calculate the discriminant b² - 4ac. If positive, two real roots; if zero, one real root; if negative, complex roots. Finally, apply the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. These points could be maxima, minima, or points of inflection depending on the second derivative test.
